source.author: سبا حیدرخانی

source.title: جهش قیمت‌های دارو در ایران پس از جنگ؛ از انسولین تا داروهای قلبی
X post: steel retirees in Tehran and Isfahan protested cutoff of supplementary insurance
X post: Tehran water reportedly cut for eight daytime hours

claim.statement: On 29 April 2026, Iran International reported that about 5,000 branded drug items had changed price, a review of roughly 200 items showed increases up to 380%, and 46 sampled drugs averaged 107% growth; reported examples included Iranian insulin pens rising from 205,000 to 640,000 toman and foreign Novomix/Novorapid from 240,000 to 890,000 toman.
claim.subject: Iran drug market
claim.object: thousands of medicines with triple-digit increases

evidence.summary: Iran International reported 5,000 branded drug price changes, up to 380% increases in a 200-item review, 107% average growth for 46 drugs, and specific insulin price jumps.
Radio Farda, citing ILNA field reporting, described insulin and metformin scarcity and multi-fold price increases, including Osvix rising from 280-320k toman to 1.2M toman.

information_depth.rationale: Multiple Persian reports provide item-level price figures and market-wide repricing counts.

claim.statement: On 20 April 2026, Aftab/ILNA reported patient-level insulin access stress across multiple cities: Lantus was hard to find in Tehran, patients in Bijar and Mianeh reported failing to buy needed insulin, a Shahin Shahr patient said she visited seven pharmacies and rationed doses out of fear of running out, and a Bandar Anzali patient said his usual pharmacy had received no insulin since before Nowruz.
claim.subject: Iranian diabetic patients
claim.object: hard insulin access and dose rationing

evidence.summary: Aftab/ILNA included named patient anecdotes from Shahin Shahr and Bandar Anzali plus reports from Tehran, Bijar, and Mianeh; it also cited 3-4x price increases for test strips and sensors rising to 16-20M toman.

information_depth.rationale: Includes direct patient accounts, city names, concrete medication names, and equipment prices.

claim.statement: On 29 April 2026, HRANA/Melliun reported at least four labor/pensioner protest actions: steel-industry retirees gathered in Isfahan and Tehran over a nine-day lapse in supplementary medical insurance, while railway infrastructure workers in Dorud, Lorestan and Andimeshk protested for a second consecutive day over neglected arrears and customary benefits; workers said 400-500 people were employed in Dorud alone and contractor workers had been excluded from wartime aid given to administrative staff.
claim.subject: Iranian steel retirees and railway infrastructure workers
claim.object: insurance lapse, arrears, and benefit exclusion

evidence.summary: HRANA/Melliun reported steel retiree gatherings in Isfahan and Tehran plus second-day protests by railway infrastructure workers in Dorud and Andimeshk.
xPool found an April 30 Persian X post repeating the steel-retiree protest claim and stating retirees demanded restoration of supplementary insurance.

information_depth.rationale: Specific date, places, groups, demands, and worker-count detail from HRANA/ILNA, with xPool social corroboration.

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026, xPool surfaced a Persian X post complaining that despite heavy rain in Tehran, water had been cut for eight hours during the day; this is a low-confidence ground signal consistent with other reports of informal Tehran water restrictions, not independently verified evidence of citywide service status.
claim.subject: Tehran water service
claim.object: cut for eight daytime hours by one X user

evidence.summary: The X post said that in Tehran, despite rainfall, water was cut for eight hours during the day.

information_depth.rationale: Single social post found through xPool; useful as ground texture but not independently verified.

assessment.uncertainty: Treat as anecdotal evidence only unless corroborated by additional local posts or service notices.

question.text: Do medicine price shocks and insulin shortages produce organized patient protests around the Food and Drug Administration, hospitals, or insurers?
question.why_it_matters: Patient-led mobilization would broaden the current labor/pensioner protest map into a direct health-access legitimacy crisis.

question.text: Are labor and pensioner protests shifting from wage-only grievances toward health-insurance and treatment-access demands?
question.why_it_matters: A benefits-to-healthcare shift would connect economic unrest with the drug and hospital-access crisis.

operations.rationale: The repricing data quantifies and broadens the prior claim that ordinary illness is becoming unaffordable.
Insulin search/rationing is a concrete patient-level example of the medicine access squeeze.
The Apr 29 steel-retiree and railway-worker actions extend the multi-city wage/benefits protest pattern.
The new protests are a current instance inside the broader HRANA-documented labor/guild unrest trend.
The social post is weak corroborating texture for informal Tehran water cuts.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v6 — medicine squeeze meets benefits unrest
synthesis.summary: The sixth pass adds sharper health-system and benefits signals. The medicine crisis is now measurable beyond generic scarcity: Persian reports describe about 5,000 drug items repriced, sampled increases up to 380%, Iranian insulin pens rising from 205k to 640k toman, foreign Novomix/Novorapid from 240k to 890k, and 46 drugs averaging 107% growth. Patient-level reporting from Tehran, Bijar, Mianeh, Shahin Shahr, and Bandar Anzali shows insulin scarcity forcing pharmacy searches, substitute insulin, and dose rationing. On the labor side, Apr 29 steel-retiree protests in Isfahan and Tehran over a nine-day supplementary-insurance lapse, plus second-day railway-worker protests in Dorud and Andimeshk over arrears/benefits, suggest the wage-protest field is bleeding into medical-coverage survival. xPool adds one low-confidence Tehran water-cut anecdote, useful only as texture. Net: the current crack map is no longer just food, wages, internet, and elite bargaining; medicine access and health-insurance loss are becoming daily-life pressure points that can connect retirees, patients, workers, and households.
synthesis.limitations: Medicine-price reports are strong on item-level examples but still need systematic official price-table or pharmacy-scrape verification. The xPool Tehran water item is a single social post and should not be treated as verified citywide evidence.

operations.reason: v6 adds quantified medicine repricing, insulin access/rationing, benefits-linked labor protests, and one low-confidence xPool water signal.
